Polestar Formula 2030 Concept Breaks Cover, Looks Futuristic in the Healthiest Way Possible
54 photos
Photo: Polestar
What you see is what you're going to get with the new Formula 2030 concept car from Polestar. Meaning, future models from the Swedish brand will be inspired by what we're seeing here today, and we've already received confirmation that among those models will be the upcoming Polestar 7 and the next-generation Polestar 2.
Just when you thought things couldn't get more futuristic than the Polestar 5, here comes this concept with a roof height of just 1,350 mm (53.1 in) - even lower than that of the previously mentioned model. The Formula 2030 concept also happens to be 4.68 meters (184 in) long, about 2 meters (78.7 in) wide, and has a 2.78 meter-long (109.4 in) wheelbase. It's a somewhat compact four-door "sports car", according to Polestar. Yes, they used the term sports car, not us.
To me, it looks more like a compact four-door GT car. A smaller and more neatly packaged version of the ridiculously expensive Polestar 5 . By the way, could this be the body style of the future on all non-SUV models? There's a good chance that it will be, because the traditional three-box sedan shape isn't the most practical. Feel free to travel around western Europe, especially in Italy and Spain, and you'll notice how hatchbacks and wagons outnumber sedans by the millions.
The side profile tells you everything you need to know with that classic cab rearward stance extending into those powerful rear haunches. Then you've got the long hood, short overhands, the 22" wheels, coke bottle hips, and the signature Dual Blade headlights. This is instantly recognizable as a Polestar , and it looks like it belongs both in the future and in an alternate reality (in like a safe version of Gotham City).
Also, notice how there's no longer a light bar at the rear? That's right, future Polestar models will come with these Single Blade rear lights which look way better. I'll go for split taillights over a light bar any day of the week. The latter just lacks character. By the way, the exterior color you're seeing here is brand new and it's called Nitrogen.
Photo: Polestar So basically, this is what you want from an EV , isn't it? To look futuristic in a healthy way, instead of a controversial way where you're trying to reinvent the wheel just for the sake of doing something different. German carmakers could stand to learn a thing or two from this recipe, Mercedes in particular.
"We wanted to evolve, while respecting, the core design values we demonstrated with previous models that define the Polestar brand in such a recognizable way. And with Formula 2030, with its clear Polestar design attributes like the Dual Blade headlights, wraparound visor-like windscreen and powerful haunches, we have done just that," said company design boss, Nahum Escobedo.
"But we've pushed perceptions, preconceptions and the expected as well, with our considered choices in form language, amplification of the performance topic and new detailing like the Single Blade rear lights."
Moving along to the interior, once you open those "opposing" doors, you'll immediately notice the pillarless design giving you easy access to the four seats. The cockpit itself appears to be somewhat driver-focused, and you get a 20" HyperDIM curved display mounted directly to the steering column. The 12.2" infotainment display is integrated into the center tunnel and you can lower it when you don't need it.
Photo: Polestar The driver can select between three modes in Performance, Normal and Autonomous. We needn't explain what they do. However, I will touch on that steering wheel design, because yokes are still controversial. This one, however, looks way more ergonomic than most - especially compared to what Tesla did on the Model S and Model X.
Polestar currently has five models in its lineup: The 2, 3, 4 coupe, 4 SUV, and the 5. Upcoming models include the 2's successor (2027), a 2028-bound Polestar 7 compact SUV, and the Polestar 6 roadster.
